name: Pan-European nationalism
summary: Pan-European nationalism holds that the peoples of Europe form one nation that should have one government and be independent of both the United States and the Soviet Union. The postwar movement was an anti-liberal and anti-communist far right: its main strands, Mosley's Europe a Nation, Yockey's Imperium and Thiriart's Jeune Europe, agree on union, an armed third force, a self-sufficient Europe-Africa bloc and separation of Europeans from non-Europeans, and differ on democracy, class and the Soviet Union.
scope: The nationalism of the European nation itself, 1945 to the 1970s: Oswald Mosley's Europe a Nation (Union Movement, Europe: Faith and Plan 1958), the 1962 Declaration of Venice of the National Party of Europe (signed by Union Movement, Jeune Europe, Reichspartei and others), Yockey's Imperium and the European Liberation Front's Proclamation of London, Thiriart's Jeune Europe and the 1950-51 Rome/Malmo programme of the European Social Movement. Positions stated by one strand only are left null, or are a split where another strand states the opposite; the economic and social programmes of the parties that carried it count only where these texts state them as part of the European cause. It excludes pro-EU federalism and later Eurosceptic or Identitarian movements.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Venice insists Europe be strongly armed, and Thiriart writes that a nation without an army exists only as fiction and there will be no Europe without a European army.

arms-reduction.rationale: Mosley calls disarmament the most desirable thing on earth, to come by mutual inspection, and Venice commits European leadership to mutual disarmament, but only after Europe is matched with the other powers.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Venice has elections that all parties may enter, but Thiriart treats communist agents as agents of an enemy power to be dealt with as such.

central-planning.rationale: Thiriart compares capitalist and collectivist production and finds capitalism's results overwhelmingly better, and Venice's wage-price leadership is a guidance of a free economy, not planning by the state.

civilizational-union.rationale: The Declaration of Venice founds the union on one European civilisation drawn from Greece and Rome, Yockey's Proclamation of London on the unity of the Western Culture, and the Malmo programme on defending western culture through a European nation.

class-collaboration.rationale: Yockey calls class-war a disease of the nation, and Venice and Mosley build a producers' state in which government wage-price leadership makes ownership quarrels irrelevant.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Yockey calls the Marxist reading of history as class struggle ludicrously simple and class war a Culture-disease, and Venice calls ownership controversies a nineteenth-century matter.

common-currency.rationale: The 1950 Malmo programme gives the European Nation a common customs and monetary system, and Venice puts finance in one European government.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Thiriart calls competition a hard but fruitful law that rewards effort, and Yockey treats struggle between peoples as the stuff of history.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Mosley says European government must be chosen and dismissed by free vote, but Thiriart denies popular sovereignty is authority and Yockey bases authority on Destiny, so the texts differ.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Thiriart and Yockey attack advertising, comfort and money-worship, but Mosley wants mass consumption to match mass production and calls the desire to earn for one's family honourable.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Venice and Mosley have government set wages and prices with unions as an estate of the realm, while Thiriart condemns corporatism and wants independent unions.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Thiriart says only Europe possesses civilisation, the United States and Russia holding only a civilisation derived from it, and Venice credits European civilisation with giving thought, beauty, science and leadership to mankind.

defeat-communism.rationale: Venice pledges mutual help against communism and Thiriart wants Soviet power rolled back, but Mosley proposes letting each civilisation develop separately in its own area and winning the argument by debate.

democracy-best.rationale: Mosley and the Malmo programme require free elections and dismissal of governments by free vote, but Thiriart calls democracy the right of lice to eat lions and Yockey rejects democracy as a spent nineteenth-century outlook.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Venice and Mosley describe Marxist communist rule as bureaucratic tyranny and a Marxian-inspired dictatorship to be resisted.

direct-action.rationale: Thiriart prepares insurrection and revolutionary action, but Mosley wants Europe made through votes in the national electorates.

direct-votes.rationale: The Union Movement's scheme called for referendums to accept or reject a strong executive, but Thiriart calls referendums on European unity naive.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Mosley campaigned for a ban on mixed-race marriages, Thiriart defends a white community's refusal to mix, and Venice rejects a complete mixture of peoples as neither desirable nor possible.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Venice says multi-racial government breaks down everywhere, Thiriart warns that integration produces a sub-proletariat and race war, and Mosley foresees an endless heritage of racial hatred if the races share one state.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Yockey puts Duty and Discipline above whining for rights, but Mosley says liberty is a basic need and the Malmo programme makes freedoms inviolable.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Mosley's central economic plan is a Europe-Africa economy insulated from the world cost system, the Venice declaration claims that space for Europeans, and Thiriart says the two halves of Europe could live in almost complete autarky.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Mosley wants no power to suspend the ban on imprisonment without trial even in popular fear, but Yockey says a sovereign state has an organic right to determine and strike the inner enemy.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Venice says Europe's rise as a third power ends the political and military power of the UN, and Thiriart dismisses the League of Nations as a farce that the awakening of Europe will end.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Malmo programme guarantees equality of individuals before the law, while Venice and Thiriart deny non-Europeans political rights in Europe and treat races as unequal, so the texts point both ways.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Mosley says a decisive system of differential rewards must relate reward to effort, and Yockey counterposes Hierarchy to Equality.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Venice and Thiriart want a European nation of one stock, with non-Europeans denied political rights; the 1950 Malmo programme instead lets colonial peoples join the European Nation as equal states, so the movement's texts point both ways.

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Mosley's 'Europe a Nation and Africa the Empire of Europe', Thiriart's symbiosis of Africa with Europe, and Venice's one-third of Africa for Europeans all keep Europe's influence in former colonial lands.

free-trade.rationale: Mosley argues the only answer to world-market competition is to withdraw from world markets into a self-contained Europe-Africa economy, and Thiriart praises near-autarky for a Europe united across both halves.

gradual-change.rationale: Mosley calls for a decisive act of European government, Thiriart for revolution by an elite, and Yockey for a Declaration of War, none of them for gradual change within existing institutions.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Mosley wants reward directly related to effort, and Thiriart wants property moved from speculation to production.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Venice says Europe must be as strongly armed as America or Russia and has nuclear production confined to the three great powers, so Europe has its own; Thiriart objects to a NATO nuclear monopoly held by the USA.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Mosley says the West must arm as long as the Russians arm and match them in decisive weapons, and Venice keeps Europe as strongly armed as America or Russia until mutual disarmament is secured.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Thiriart says nation is a shared historical destiny, not language or race, and calls language nationalism no better than race nationalism; Yockey's Proclamation reduces English, German, French and Italian to 'linguistic variations' inside one European nation.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Thiriart treats free enterprise as the most efficient means, but Mosley and Venice give government economic leadership over wages and prices.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Yockey says Marx made all culture a reflection of economics, which he finds amazing anyone took seriously, and Venice condemns 'destructive materialism'.

multipolar-world.rationale: Venice says Europe's emergence as a third great power ends the UN's role so that three great powers deal directly with each other, and Mosley presents Europe as a third force between American money and Soviet mob.

national-rebirth.rationale: Yockey's Proclamation names the cleansing of the European soul and the building of the Imperium as its two tasks, Thiriart calls for a revolutionary elite to replace 'degenerate' parliamentary democracy, and Venice attacks present 'division, delay and subservience'.

natural-rulers.rationale: Thiriart builds the state on a rare elite of excellent men fitted for power and Yockey counterposes Hierarchy to Equality.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Venice sets out a 'third system' producers' state superior to both American capitalism and communist tyranny, Thiriart rejects both mercantile capitalism and communism, and Yockey rejects both as nineteenth-century outlooks.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Venice gives the European government foreign policy, defence, economic leadership, finance and science, and Mosley gives it sole responsibility for finance and wage-price leadership.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Venice makes the immediate withdrawal of Russian and American forces and military bases from Europe a primary object of European government, and Yockey calls all extra-European forces on European soil enemies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Venice and Mosley require elections that any party may enter and Mosley discards the totalitarian party, but Thiriart says those who fought for the new order alone should hold all levers of the state, citing the single party.

open-borders.rationale: Venice, Mosley's repatriation campaign and Yockey's call to expel everything alien from European soil leave no room for open borders; only Europeans are to move freely within Europe.

organic-representation.rationale: Mosley and the Malmo programme favour occupational electoral districts, while Thiriart condemns envious, limited corporatism.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Venice presents the National Party of Europe as combining patriotism and progress for a producers' state, and Yockey calls socialism the principle of each for all.

person-over-state.rationale: Thiriart wants liberty of the person and the state only so far as it protects goods, while Yockey makes the State an organism above individuals.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Thiriart calls the 'European' politicians unfit and a parliamentary democracy corrupted by degenerate liberalism, and Yockey brands party politicians and the 'inner enemy' traitors.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The 1962 Declaration of Venice (signed by Union Movement, Jeune Europe, Reichspartei and others) puts foreign policy, defence, economic policy, finance and science in one elected European government over national parliaments, and the 1950-51 Rome/Malmo programme made a European nation its first duty.

population-transfer.rationale: Mosley's Union Movement campaigned for mandatory repatriation of black immigrants and Yockey demands the complete expulsion of the alien from European soil, though neither frames the minority as hostile.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Venice says the splendour of Europe's history and the nobility of its traditions must never be surrendered, in the nation Europe a Nation would make of the continent.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Thiriart will tolerate only a capitalism serving the European nation, and Yockey's socialism says a man working for himself alone works against the good of all.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Venice pledges to be true to fellow Europeans, particularly where threatened in Africa, and Thiriart dedicates his book to the hundred million Europeans held under Soviet rule whom he vows to liberate.

public-ownership.rationale: Venice prefers workers' ownership or syndicalism to state bureaucracy for already nationalised industries, and Thiriart says state ownership of the means of production is costly and abolishes freedom.

race-social-construct.rationale: Thiriart calls denial of racial differences ridiculous and says they rest on experimentally demonstrated ethnological data, and Venice speaks of a European communion of blood.

racial-franchise.rationale: Venice and Thiriart deny political rights to the other race in each other's territory, but the Malmo programme grants free elections and equality before the law, so the texts point both ways.

racial-pride.rationale: Venice declares 'with pride' a European communion of blood and spirit and treats the heritage of Europe as never to be surrendered.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Venice and Thiriart want races kept in separate states with 'clean settlement of clear division', but the Malmo programme guarantees equality of individuals before the law, so the movement's texts point both ways on segregation law.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Yockey's Proclamation names rationalism among the dross to be cleansed from the European soul and puts Faith among the European values, and the Malmo programme makes the rebirth of Christianity the foundation of revival.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Mosley's Union Movement campaigned for compulsory repatriation of Caribbean immigrants, Venice denies non-Europeans political rights in Europe, and Yockey demands the expulsion of everything alien from European soil.

religion-illusion.rationale: Yockey says religion is a necessity for cultured man, and the Malmo programme makes the rebirth of Christianity the foundation of European revival.

religious-nation.rationale: Thiriart sees no reason to exclude Europeans for their religion, while the Malmo programme makes Christianity the foundation of renewal and Mosley says his creed can be held in any church or none.

restore-past-order.rationale: Venice says the party must never be misrepresented as a policy of reaction, Thiriart calls his anti-communism not reactionary or backward-looking, and Yockey says History cannot go backward.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Mosley says withdrawal of the powers would make a united Germany inevitable within the union of Europe, and Thiriart wants Yalta undone and the two halves of Europe fused.

right-to-secede.rationale: Thiriart says the parts of a nation have no separate existence of their own, and Yockey calls anyone who perpetuates petty-statism the inner enemy of Europe.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Yockey grounds the European mission in a divinely emanated soul, Mosley's doctrine of higher forms fights all-prevailing materialism, and Venice speaks of a communion of blood and of spirit.

state-harmful.rationale: Yockey's Imperium and Proclamation treat the sovereign State as the organism of politics, and Mosley says power must be used by some people somewhere in a modern society.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Venice casts Europe as a third power independent of both the American and Soviet blocs, Yockey says Europe will never fight for any extra-European force, and Thiriart rules out a classical alliance with the USA.

strong-leader.rationale: Mosley wants an elected executive able to act without delay and bypass parliament on finance (though no single dictator), while Yockey and Thiriart want authority and a leading elite.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Mosley and the Malmo programme forbid suppressing opposition propaganda, but Yockey's Proclamation vows to grind the inner enemy into the dirt.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Venice claims the space of a united Europe including liberated eastern lands, the dominions and about a third of Africa, Yockey proclaims a European will to unlimited political imperialism, and Thiriart's Europe runs from Brest to Bucharest.

traditional-family.rationale: Thiriart calls the family the base cell of a solid society whose destruction opens the door to neuroses, and Yockey lists family among the higher unities against social atomism.

worker-ownership.rationale: Venice and Mosley prefer worker ownership for nationalised or mature industries, but Thiriart favours co-ownership of the production's profits and opposes co-ownership of the means of production.

missingStatements.text: Government should adjust wages and prices so that people can buy what the economy produces.
missingStatements.rationale: The wage-price mechanism is the core economic aim of Mosley's Europe a Nation and the fourth aim of the Declaration of Venice.
missingStatements.declined: Theory wording a general reader would need explained.

missingStatements.text: Black and white peoples should live in separate states, with neither holding political rights in the other's territory.
missingStatements.rationale: The Declaration of Venice and Thiriart both propose clean territorial separation of the races and no political rights for either in the other's land.

notes: Strands: Mosley's Europe a Nation (a unitary elected government with national parliaments for social and cultural matters, free elections, state economic leadership, racial separation); Yockey (an Imperium that abolishes the nations, rejects democracy and liberalism, and tactically favoured the USSR); Thiriart (a unitary European state led by a revolutionary elite, free enterprise as a means, independent unions, anti-Soviet in 1964 and later national-communist); the Malmo programme (a federal European Nation of equal states, Christian, free elections, equality of white and colored peoples). Where these disagree the answer is 0 at low confidence; positions stated by one strand only are null. Themes searched: economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, means, globalism. Positions on ecology, technology, gender, drugs, policing and most economic policy are not stated in these texts. Blocked: Britannica's Mosley entry and academia.edu (Cloudflare challenge), Taylor and Francis article on the European far right's geopolitics (403), Charles University thesis on Mosley's Europe (no connection); Thiriart's English translation and Mosley's 'The Alternative' (1947), 'Mosley: Right or Wrong?' and 'My Life' were not available as full text and the main gap is Mosley's postwar pamphlets and the Union Movement's own programmes. Review (2026-10-30): unions-good, collective-bargaining, farm-price-support and regulate-corporations nulled under the scope rule, as in arab-nationalism.
